HW1 · The loop, MVC, and orientation

Out Thursday October 8 · due Wednesday October 14, 11:59 PM on Canvas · 2.5 % of the course grade · Unity or WebGL · hub · schedule · syllabus · all homework
Read before this homework: Unity for This Course §4, the lifecycle and the two clocks · §7, the math types · §11, implement and replace · Interactive Systems §1 to §3 (the loop, the timestep, MVC) · Affine Transformations §6, TRS

What you build

Three small functions behind the first thing every interactive graphics program does: move something every frame at a speed that does not depend on the frame rate, turn a model's three numbers into the matrix the view draws with, and aim an object at a target. The runner draws a cube with your matrix (the sliders are the controller, the numbers the model, the cube and the matrix card two views of it) and an arrow aimed by your basis at a ball your loop moves.

JavaScriptC#What it computes
advanceAdvancep + velocity · dt: one frame of motion; velocity is per second, dt in seconds.
trsMatrixTrsMatrixT(t) · Ry(ry) · S(s, s, s) as a 4 × 4, built entry by entry. Column 0 is where the x axis lands, column 3 is t.
orientBasisOrientBasisThe unit axes {x, y, z} of an object at pos whose +z points at target: z = normalize(target − pos), x = normalize(up × z), y = z × x.
  • Angles in degrees; Ry has column 0 = (cos, 0, −sin), the right-handed formula, which is also what Unity's own y rotation stores.
  • WebGL: matrices are column-major 16-arrays, entry (row r, column c) at index c · 4 + r. Unity: Matrix4x4 is indexed m[row, col].
  • The two advance checks call your function 60 times with dt = 1/60 and 20 times with dt = 1/20; both must land at the same place.

Implement and replace

Build each function from primitives (dot, cross, normalize, subtraction, component access, + − × ÷, sin and cos.) and use the engine's own helper, where one exists, only to check your result. These are off limits in your submission:

TrackOff limits
WebGL (JavaScript)makeTRS from xform.js; THREE.Matrix4.compose, makeRotationY, lookAt; Object3D.lookAt; any Quaternion.
Unity (C#)Matrix4x4.TRS, Matrix4x4.Rotate; Quaternion.Euler, AngleAxis, LookRotation; Transform.LookAt, Transform.Rotate.

Getting started

WebGL track.
  1. Download the course site: its repository (Code, then Download ZIP), or git clone it.
  2. From the site's root folder run python3 -m http.server 8000 and open http://localhost:8000/homework/run.html?hw=hw01.
  3. Edit lib/skeletons/hw01.js, the only file you change, and reload: the Checks table under the scene compares your numbers with the ones below.

The unfilled skeleton runs on this site too, so you can see the page before you start.

Unity track.
  1. In Unity Hub, create a new project with the 3D (Built-In Render Pipeline) template in editor 6000.3.11f1.
  2. From the same download, copy the files in homework/hw01/unity/ into Assets/HW01/.
  3. Create an empty GameObject, add the Checks component (namespace CSS551.HW01), and press Play: the Console lists every check with your value and the expected one.
  4. Edit HW01.cs; the other files are given.

The Unity files compile against a stand-in for the UnityEngine API and pass their checks with the reference solution, but they are new this quarter and have not yet been opened in the Unity editor. If one does not compile in 6000.3.11f1, post the error on the Canvas board and use the WebGL track meanwhile.

Submitting and grading

  • WebGL: the one file hw01.js.
  • Unity: the project folder, zipped, without Library/, Temp/, Logs/ and obj/.

Grading runs your functions twice: on the published inputs above and on a second set of inputs that is not published. A check earns its points only when your value is within its tolerance on both, so the numbers have to come from the math. The score is the sum of the points earned, out of 100. A submission that does not load or compile earns no check points. Name any collaborators and tools in the submission comment.

Late tokens. You have two for the quarter. Declare one in the submission comment to extend this homework by 24 hours without penalty. Beyond tokens, late homework loses 10 % per day for up to three days.
